items.summary: BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCache returns ~98.5% wrong elements on windows-gfx1151 (ROCm 7.14, clang 23) while rope/estimate pass and the same branch passes on gfx1100/gfx90a at ROCm 7.2.3; not aliasing, not -O3 (both rebuilt and retested)

PORT DEFECT (supersedes quest-gfx1151-decode-attn-wrong, which wrongly blamed ROCm). Under HIP __CUDACC_VER_MAJOR__ is undefined, so FLASHINFER_CP_ASYNC_ENABLED is off and cp_async commit_group/wait_group compile to empty, leaving the decode kernel 2-stage smem pipeline with no ordering. Races at >=4 wavefronts per block: wrong on gfx1151, LATENT on gfx90a/gfx1100 which currently pass by scheduling luck. Proven: num_stages_smem=1 gives 121/121; bdz 1/2/4 pass, bdz=8 fails. Fix = shim cp_async.cuh, or force single-stage on the HIP path

FIXED in 9be60fc. The sparse decode kernel's single-block launch shape is broken: it runs with gridDim.x==1 where the slice-length expression (batch_idx == gridDim.x-1 ? last_page_len : page_size) always picks last_page_len, collapsing the block's KV slice. Only reachable when num_kv_heads saturates the occupancy grid, i.e. on low-CU parts -- gfx1151 (20 CUs) hit it, gfx1100 (70) and gfx942 (304) never did. Correcting that one expression is NOT sufficient; the path has at least one further defect, so it is disabled rather than repaired. Left open for a porter who wants to repair and re-enable it

RULED now by Jeff Daily 2026-08-19, to be done in the same porting round as quest-decode-single-block-path-broken. 9be60fc disables the single-block decode path with a plain 'constexpr bool kSingleBlockPathIsCorrect = false' in the shared kernels/include/decode/decode_attn.cuh, with no HIP guard, so CUDA builds take it too. The selecting condition (batch_size * num_kv_heads >= blocks_per_cu * cu_count) is reachable on a low-SM NVIDIA card, so the change alters NVIDIA launch behaviour under a [ROCm] commit prefix, and nothing about the defect is HIP-specific. Compounding it, the CUDA no-regression gate is recorded cuda-not-validated at this head (RAFT branch-24.02 CUDA::nvToolsExt wall), so the CUDA path is not even compile-checked. Decision: keep the CUDA path at upstream behaviour. If the single-block path is successfully repaired and re-enabled, this resolves itself; if any disable survives the repair, it must be HIP-guarded.
